newsitem.title: UK: Base metals quiet, LME nickel slips after stocks.
newsitem.headline: Base metals quiet, LME nickel slips after stocks.

text.p: Base metals generally held steady levels during thin early London Metal Exchange (LME) trading on Friday, though nickel eased following a a sizeable inventory rise of 1,872 tonnes.

Three months delivery nickel was last trading at $7,330, down on its high of $7,360 and Thursday's LME kerb close of $7,380. Traders said the market was finding robust underlying support and was unlikely to show any significant losses following its recent sharp rally of over $1,000. During the early part of 1997 prices have moved from a low of around $6,400 to a four-month peak of $7,490.
Traders said the rise in nickel stocks had been expected following market rumours on Thursday. They said the material was attracted to LME warehouses after the recent impressive gains.

LME stock data showed that 1,344 tonnes of nickel was delivered in Rotterdam warehouses, possibly of Russian origin which has recently been cut. Copper absorbed an expected stocks rise of 7,025 tonnes and was last at $2,254, up $6. Traders said copper was expected to consolidate between $2,230 and $2,290 near-term. It is likely to find support from tight nearby spreads. Cash to three months was indicated at $185 against $175/$180.
Aluminium continued to find good support above $1,600 and managed to absorb a stocks rise.

Traders said aluminium was likely to consolidate on Friday and pegged resistance at $1,625/30. Zinc after a stocks fall moved to $1,129, up $9, while lead was up $3 at $713 and was also benefiting from an inventory decline.
Alloy was indicated at $1,510/20, against $1,510/12. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8075
